renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: profiler_embedding
  title: Profiler ordination
  description: |-
    Each point is one profiling run, a sample classified by one profiler and database, placed by the Bray-Curtis distance between taxon abundance profiles and coloured by profiler. It answers whether the profilers describe the same community or disagree.
    How to read: runs that sit together report similar communities, so a tight cluster of profilers agrees. A profiler that lands apart from the others reports a different set of taxa or names them differently, so open the detection overlap and the taxon by run matrix to see which taxa drive the gap. Runs of one profiler from different samples spread apart when the samples differ biologically.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The axes are principal coordinates of the Bray-Curtis matrix, so only distances between points carry meaning.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PCo
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: profiler

- component: table
  title: Profiling run coordinates
  description: |-
    Each row is one profiling run, a sample classified by one profiler and database, with its two ordination coordinates and the platform it was sequenced on. It answers where a given run sits in the ordination.
    How to read: sort by a coordinate to find the runs at either extreme, then filter to a profiler to compare its runs across samples.

- component: card
  title: Profiling runs
  description: |-
    Each unit is one profiling run, a sample classified by one profiler and database, and the ring splits the runs by sequencing platform. The second number counts the distinct profiler and database pairs. It answers how much of the ordination each platform contributes.
    How to read: a ring dominated by one platform means the ordination mostly compares runs of that platform, so profiler differences may partly be platform differences.
  column: profiler_db
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: platform
  caption: runs, by sequencing platform

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lineage_sunburst
  title: Taxonomic hierarchy
  description: |-
    Each arc is a taxon: the rings run from superkingdom at the centre to species at the edge, sized by the summed relative abundance of the profiling runs in view and coloured by phylum. It answers which lineages dominate the community the profilers report.
    How to read: a wide arc at an inner ring means that lineage holds most of the abundance, and its children show how it splits. Reads no profiler could place keep their own unclassified branch, so a large one means the database misses much of the sample. Filter to one profiler to compare its hierarchy with another.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. Arc sizes add the relative abundances of every run in view, so filter to a single run for shares that sum to one.
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: phylum
  roles:
    ranks:
    - superkingdom
    - phylum
    - class
    - order
    - family
    - genus
    - species
    abundance: rel_abundance

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lineage_sankey
  title: Taxonomic flow
  description: |-
    Each band is a group of taxa flowing from the root through superkingdom and phylum down to genus, sized by the summed relative abundance of the runs in view. It answers how the community divides at each rank and where the unclassified reads leave the tree.
    How to read: a thick band from the root into one superkingdom means that domain dominates. A band that splits into many thin ones at the genus step marks a diverse phylum. Compare a profiler with a large unclassified band against one with a small band to see how much each database covers.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. Band widths add the relative abundances of every run in view.
  kind: sankey
  config:
    color_mode: target
    value_col: rel_abundance
    value_label: Summed relative abundance
  roles:
    steps:
    - root
    - superkingdom
    - phylum
    - genus

- component: card
  title: Distinct species
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct species reported, the second number counts every species row, and the bars rank the phyla by how many rows they hold. It answers how rich the profiles are and which phyla contribute most.
    How to read: a few phyla holding most of the rows is the usual shape of a mock or low-complexity community. Rows without a placed phylum are left out of the ranking.
  column: species
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: phylum
  top_n_count: 4
  filter_expr: (col('phylum') != 'unclassified') & (col('phylum') != 'unresolved')
  caption: species rows, by the richest phyla

- component: card
  title: Typical taxon abundance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median relative abundance of a taxon in a run, with the smallest and largest below it, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how evenly the abundance is spread over the reported taxa.
    How to read: a distribution piled near zero with a long right tail means a few taxa dominate over a long tail of rare ones. The values span orders of magnitude, so the histogram reads better filtered to one profiler.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: relative abundance of every taxon

- component: card
  title: Distinct phyla
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct phyla reported, and the bars rank the superkingdoms by how many phylum rows they hold. It answers which domains of life the profilers place their taxa in.
    How to read: a ranking led by Bacteria with a short Archaea bar is typical. Compare profilers with the filters to see which ones reach a domain the others miss.
  column: phylum
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: superkingdom
  top_n_count: 4
  filter_expr: (col('phylum') != 'unclassified') & (col('phylum') != 'unresolved')
  caption: phylum rows, by domain of life

- component: card
  title: Largest taxon share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest relative abundance any taxon reaches in a run, with the median below it, and the histogram shows all values. It answers whether one taxon dominates a profile.
    How to read: a maximum far above the median means one taxon takes a large share of the run. It is a fraction of the run's total, so a high value also follows from a profile reporting few taxa.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: relative abundance of every taxon

- component: interactive
  title: Superkingdom
  description: Filters every tile of this view to the chosen superkingdoms. It answers whether a pattern
    holds within one domain of life.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: superkingdom

- component: interactive
  title: Phylum
  description: Filters every tile of this view to the chosen phyla. It answers which phyla drive a profile.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: phylum

- component: table
  title: Lineage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon reported by one profiler in one sample, with its seven NCBI ranks, its read count and its relative abundance. It answers which lineage a given taxon belongs to and how abundant it is.
    How to read: sort by relative abundance to see the leading taxa, or filter by rank columns. Rows labelled unclassified or unresolved are reads the profiler could not place at that rank.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: concordance_heatmap
  title: Taxon by run abundance heatmap
  description: |-
    Each cell is the relative abundance of one taxon (row) in one profiling run (column), with the taxonomic rank as a row strip and the profiler and platform as column strips. It answers which taxa the profilers agree on and which runs group together.
    How to read: columns that cluster together report similar communities, and a profiler that falls on its own branch differs from the rest. A taxon bright in some columns and blank in others is detected by only some profilers, so check the detection overlap tile. Rows are the most abundant taxa, so rare taxa are not shown.
    Lines and annotations: the dendrograms come from hierarchical clustering of the rows and columns, and the strips label rank, profiler and platform.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    row_annotation_cols:
    - rank
  roles:
    index: taxon

- component: table
  title: Taxon by run table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon with its relative abundance in every profiling run, one column per run. It answers the exact value behind a heatmap cell.
    How to read: sort a run column to see its leading taxa, or filter by rank. A zero means that profiler did not report the taxon in that run.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: profiler_upset
  title: Profiler detection overlap
  description: |-
    Each bar is an intersection: the number of sample and taxon detections reported by exactly that set of profilers, coloured by how many profilers share them. It answers how much of the community the profilers agree on and how long each one's private tail is.
    How to read: tall bars with many joined dots are detections every profiler makes, so they are the safest. Tall single-dot bars are taxa only one profiler reports, which often means a database difference or a false positive. Open the cross-profiler table to see which taxa sit in a private tail.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The side bars give the total detections of each profiler.
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: card
  title: Profilers per detection
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of profilers that report a taxon in a sample, and the box shows the spread. It answers how widely a detection is shared.
    How to read: a median near the number of profilers means a consensus community. A low median with a wide box means most detections are specific to one or two profilers.
  column: n_profilers
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Detection table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon detected in a sample, with the number of profilers that report it and a 0 or 1 for each profiler. It answers which taxa a given profiler misses or reports alone.
    How to read: filter to a low profiler count to list the contested taxa, or sort by rank to compare species with genus calls.

- component: card
  title: Detected taxa
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct taxa detected, the second number counts every sample and taxon detection, and the bars rank the taxonomic ranks by detections. It answers how many taxa the profilers report together.
    How to read: a ranking led by species means the profilers resolve to species level. A large genus bar means some profilers stop at genus.
  column: taxon
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: rank
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: detections, by taxonomic rank

- component: card
  title: Widest agreement
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest count of profilers that report one taxon in one sample, with the most common count below it, and the histogram shows how many detections each count holds. It answers whether any detection is made by every profiler.
    How to read: a histogram with a bar at the maximum means a core community all profilers see, and a bar at one is the private tail.
  column: n_profilers
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: profilers per detection

- component: advanced_viz
  id: stacked_taxonomy
  title: Community composition per run
  description: |-
    Each bar is one profiler and database, split into the taxa it reports at the chosen rank and sized by relative abundance, pooling the samples in view. It answers how the community looks to each classifier.
    How to read: bars with the same colours in similar proportions agree on the community. A bar dominated by an unclassified segment points to a database that misses much of the sample, and a bar with different taxa reflects another naming vocabulary. Switch the rank, or filter to a sample, to compare like with like.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/taxprofiler/taxpasta/dev/README.md
  kind: stacked_bar
  roles:
    sample_id: profiler_db
    taxon: name
    rank: rank
    abundance: rel_abundance

- component: card
  title: Distinct taxon names
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct taxon names reported, the second number counts every row, and the ring splits distinct from repeated names. It answers how much of the vocabulary is shared between runs.
    How to read: a high share of repeated names means the profilers and samples report the same taxa. Profilers use different naming, so one organism can appear under several names.
  column: name
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: uniqueness
  caption: distinct and repeated taxon names

- component: card
  title: Assigned counts
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count assigned to taxa, with the median per row below it, and the bars rank the profilers by total. It answers how much of the data each profiler assigns.
    How to read: compare profilers with care, since each one counts its own units. The values span orders of magnitude, so a spread is not drawn.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: profiler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: assigned counts, by profiler

- component: card
  title: Samples profiled
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct samples, the second number counts every row, and the bars rank the profilers by how many taxon rows they report. It answers how many samples the table covers and which profiler reports the longest list.
    How to read: a profiler with a much longer bar reports a long tail of taxa, which may include false positives.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: profiler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: taxon rows, by profiler

- component: card
  title: Largest taxon share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest relative abundance a taxon reaches in a run, with the median below it, and the histogram shows all values. It answers whether one taxon dominates a profile.
    How to read: a maximum far above the median means one taxon takes a large share of a run. No cut-off is drawn, because no published rule separates a dominant taxon from an ordinary one.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: relative abundance of every taxon

- component: interactive
  title: Profiler
  description: Filters every tile of this view to the chosen profilers. It answers how one classifier reads
    the data on its own.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: profiler

- component: interactive
  title: Sample
  description: Filters every tile of this view to the chosen samples. It answers how the profilers behave
    on one sample.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: sample

- component: table
  title: Abundance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon reported by one profiler and database in one sample, with its rank, raw count and relative abundance. It answers the exact value behind a bar of the composition.
    How to read: sort by relative abundance for the leading taxa, or filter by rank. Relative abundance is a share of that run's total.

- component: card
  title: Rows by rank
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of rows, the second number counts the ranks present, and the bar shows the share of rows at each rank. It answers at which level the profilers report.
    How to read: a bar mostly at species means the profilers resolve to species level, and a large genus or domain share means some stop higher.
  column: rank
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: rank
  caption: rows, by taxonomic rank

- component: card
  title: Upper quartile abundance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the upper quartile of relative abundance, with the median and the largest value below it, and the histogram shows all values. It answers how abundant the commoner taxa are relative to the rarest ones.
    How to read: a quartile far below the maximum means the abundance is held by few taxa.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: q3
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: relative abundance of every taxon

- component: advanced_viz
  id: richness_dot_plot
  title: Diversity per sample and profiler
  description: |-
    Each dot is one profiling run, a sample (column) classified by one profiler and database (row). Its colour is the Shannon diversity of the profile and its size is the share held by the single top taxon. It answers which runs report a diverse community and which report one dominated by a taxon.
    How to read: large dots mean one taxon takes a big share of the profile, and pale or dark colour gives the diversity. Rows of different profilers that disagree on a sample point to a database or method difference, so compare them in the ordination. No cut-off is drawn, because no published rule separates a diverse profile from a dominated one.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: profiler_db
    mean_expression: shannon
    frac_expressing: top_taxon_fraction

- component: card
  title: Taxa observed per run
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of taxa a profiling run reports, and the box shows the spread. It answers how rich the profiles are.
    How to read: a wide box means the profilers disagree strongly on richness, so compare them with the bar chart below. A high count is not necessarily better, since a long tail of rare taxa can be false positives.
  column: taxa_observed
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Shannon diversity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean Shannon diversity of the runs, with the smallest and largest below it, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how diverse the reported communities are.
    How to read: higher values mean more taxa and a more even spread. Compare runs of the same sample, since profilers that report more rare taxa score higher. Shannon diversity has no published pass level, so no cut-off is drawn.
  column: shannon
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: Shannon diversity of every run

- component: card
  title: Pielou evenness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean Pielou evenness of the runs, and the box shows the spread. It answers whether the abundance is spread evenly over the taxa or held by a few.
    How to read: values near 1 mean an even community and values near 0 one dominated by a taxon. A low score points to a profiler that over-reports a few taxa. No cut-off is drawn, because no published rule defines a good evenness.
  column: evenness
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Profiler and database pairs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct profiler and database pairs, the second number counts every run, and the bars rank the profilers by their runs. It answers how many classifiers are compared and which ones have most runs.
    How to read: a profiler with several databases has a longer bar. Interpret comparisons across profilers with unequal run counts with care.
  column: profiler_db
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: profiler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: runs, by profiler

- component: card
  title: Assigned counts per run
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count assigned to taxa in a run, with the smallest and largest below it, and the histogram shows every run. It answers how much of the data a typical run assigns.
    How to read: the values span orders of magnitude between profilers and platforms, so read the extremes as a range and not as a spread. A very small count against the others suggests a run with little usable data.
  column: assigned_count
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: assigned counts of every run

- component: figure
  title: Richness against diversity
  description: |-
    Each point is one profiling run: the number of taxa it reports against its Shannon diversity, coloured by profiler with the sequencing platform as the marker shape. It answers whether runs that report more taxa also report a more diverse community.
    How to read: points rise together because Shannon diversity grows with richness. A profiler whose points sit above the others for the same richness has a more even profile, and one below is dominated by a few taxa. No reference line is drawn, since no published rule defines a good value.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median Shannon diversity of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of taxpasta.
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: taxa_observed
    y: shannon
    color: profiler
    symbol: platform
    labels:
      taxa_observed: Taxa observed
      shannon: Shannon diversity
      profiler: Profiler
      platform: Platform
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: shannon

- component: figure
  title: Share held by the top taxon
  description: |-
    Each box is a profiler and database: the share of each sample's profile held by its single most abundant taxon, coloured by profiler. It answers which classifiers report a few dominant taxa and which spread the community over a long tail.
    How to read: a high box means the profiles are concentrated on one taxon, and a low box a flatter profile. Filter to one sample to compare profilers on the same community, since the share depends on the community as well as on the profiler.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median share held by the top taxon of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of taxpasta.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: profiler_db
    y: top_taxon_fraction
    color: profiler
    labels:
      profiler_db: Profiler and database
      top_taxon_fraction: Share of the top taxon
      profiler: Profiler
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: top_taxon_fraction

- component: table
  title: Run statistics table
  description: |-
    Each row is one profiling run with its taxa observed, assigned count, top taxon and its share, Shannon diversity and evenness. It answers the exact values behind the tiles above.
    How to read: sort by a statistic to find the extreme runs, or filter by profiler to compare its runs.
